evidence: src/application/OrderDto.ts declares toOrderDto(order: Order): OrderDto. AdvanceOrderUseCase, CancelOrderUseCase, GetOrderUseCase, ListOrdersByStateUseCase and PlaceOrderUseCase all use it, so order mapping lives in one place.
src/application/PlaceOrderUseCase.ts calls createOrderLine and Order.place, then stock.reserve, so validation and creation stay in the domain.

src/application/CancelOrderUseCase.ts calls order.cancel() then stock.release(order.lines). src/application/AdvanceOrderUseCase.ts calls order.advanceTo(target) and, only when target is shipped, stock.dispatch. Each stock side effect appears in one use case only.

src/application/AdvanceOrderUseCase.ts, CancelOrderUseCase.ts and GetOrderUseCase.ts each repeat the guard `if (!order) throw new DomainError("not_found", ...)`. This is minor repeated boilerplate, not a duplicated domain invariant.
src/application/GetStockLevelsUseCase.ts maps Product to StockLevelDto inline. The stock read model stays inside the same module boundary.
src/application/IdGenerator.ts declares the port that PlaceOrderUseCase receives in its constructor. The port is used consistently and nothing bypasses it.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Every file in src/application belongs to one concern: the order and stock use cases, their data transfer objects (DTOs) and one port (IdGenerator). The use cases follow the same pattern. Each takes its dependencies as domain interfaces (OrderRepository, ProductRepository, StockService) and has an execute method. The order use cases all return results through the shared toOrderDto mapper; none of them builds an OrderDto inline. Domain rules stay in the domain: state transitions go through order.advanceTo and order.cancel, line validation goes through createOrderLine, and order creation goes through Order.place. Each stock side effect sits in exactly one use case: reserve in PlaceOrderUseCase, release in CancelOrderUseCase, and dispatch-on-shipped in AdvanceOrderUseCase. One weak spot: the findById-then-throw DomainError("not_found") guard is copied into three use cases. It is a small repeated guard rather than a business rule held in two places, so I did not count it as a failure, but it could move to a single helper. GetStockLevelsUseCase maps to StockLevelDto inline instead of through a mapper. This is a small style difference, not a bypass, because no stock mapper exists in the module.
